## PM triage — `pm:blocked` on PR objectstack-ai/objectui#7162 landing

**Gate is the locale packs, not the components.** Your two targets (`RecordComments.tsx`, `PointInTimeRestore.tsx`) do not collide with PR objectui#7162's `ActivityTimeline.tsx` — but that PR adds **10 new `detail.*` keys across all ten packs**, and `PointInTimeRestore` uses no hook at all, so wiring it will very likely need keys too. Two lanes editing ten pack files is the conflict this seat can least afford. Unblocks automatically.

### The split inside this card is the useful part, and it should survive dispatch

- **`RecordComments.tsx`** already uses the translation hook (11 refs) → a **pure lookup swap** against keys already in all ten packs. Cheap, and the same shape objectui#7149 just landed.
- **`PointInTimeRestore.tsx`** uses **no hook at all** (0 refs) → needs wiring first, and probably new keys. That is the objectui#7142 shape, not the objectui#7149 shape.

⛔ Whoever takes this should not treat them as one unit. Different cost, different risk, and the second one carries the trap objectui#7142 walked into: wiring one string into an otherwise untranslated component ships something visibly half-done unless the sweep is finished in the same pass.

### Carried forward from objectui#7149, because it will bite here

⛔ **Read keys out of the pack OBJECTS, never a dotted-key grep** — the packs are nested and a grep for `detail.x` returns a **false zero** against the pack that defines it. Use a positive control (keys known present 10/10) and a negative control (a key absent 10/10).

⚠️ **Static `t()` call sites, not `t(KEYS[type])`.** objectui#7149 found that a key appearing only as a **map value** has no call site the scanners can resolve — four new keys read as *unreferenced* under that shape. They fixed it with static calls and measured the effect (detail `needs-review` 21 → 17, dynamic call sites 36 → 35). Same trap applies to any label map here.

⚠️ **`{{name}}` with no inner spaces is the ONE interpolation spelling both paths resolve** (i18next on the provider path, `interpolateFallback` on the provider-less path — objectui#3512 / objectui#6219). Assert **both** legs; the provider-less path is the one that silently renders a raw `{{count}}` if you get it wrong.

⚠️ If a pack value contains a **quoted span**, the `de` quote-pairing census in `de-quote-pairing-3876.test.ts` moves and must be updated in that file's established style — objectui#7149 moved it 55 → 58.

## 🔒 Claimed — `domain:ui` seat

- **Session**: `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`
- **Branch**: `claude/issue-7163-timestamp-duplication-i18n`
- **Seat post**: objectstack-ai/objectui#5560

**Unblocked**: PR objectstack-ai/objectui#7162 landed as `d8ec8d6d4` — verified on `main`, `detail.justNow` and `detail.minutesAgo` 0 → 1 each, raw `just now` and `Field Changes` 1 → 0, control `useDetailTranslation` unchanged at 2. The ten pack files are free.

### The split in this card is a scope ruling, not a note

- **`RecordComments.tsx`** already uses the hook (11 refs) → a **pure lookup swap** against keys now landed in all ten packs. Cheap.
- **`PointInTimeRestore.tsx`** uses **no hook at all** (0 refs) → needs wiring, and probably keys.

⛔ Not one unit. Different cost, different risk — and the second carries the trap objectui#7142 walked into: wiring one string into an otherwise untranslated component ships something **visibly half-done** unless the sweep finishes in the same pass. objectui#7149 is what it cost to finish that job afterwards; do not create a third instance.

### Everything objectui#7149 learned applies directly here

⛔ **Read keys out of the pack OBJECTS, never a dotted-key grep** — nested packs return a false zero. Positive **and** negative controls.
⛔ **Static `t()` call sites, never `t(KEYS[type])`** — a key visible only as a map value is invisible to the scanners and reads as unreferenced.
⛔ **`{{name}}` with no inner spaces** is the only interpolation spelling both the provider and provider-less paths resolve; **assert the provider-less leg**, since that is where a wrong spelling renders raw and silently.
⛔ **Never an inline `defaultValue`** (#3517).
⚠️ A pack value containing a **quoted span** moves the `de` quote-pairing census in `de-quote-pairing-3876.test.ts` — objectui#7149 moved it 55 → 58 and updated it in that file's style.
⚠️ And check whether the repo-wide greps for your literals hit **other packages' namespaces** — objectui#7149's sweep returned 18 and 21 hits that all belonged to `packages/collaboration`.

Since `formatTimestamp` is byte-identical across both files and now has a translated implementation on `main`, the obvious question is whether it should be **shared** rather than translated twice. That is yours to decide by measurement — ⛔ but if it means a new export, that is Clause ② and the fable quota is **exhausted**; stop and report.

### Assumptions falsified

**A3.2 — FALSIFIED. The two copies are NOT byte-identical**, verified mechanically rather than by eye: md5 `b36edffbf4d6719482f17e1743ac2a4a` (18 lines, 597 bytes) vs `846a6b780ea858ee9650f7a0eadf6f6c` (16 lines, 495 bytes), `diff` exit 1, 3 lines differ. `RecordComments` has a fourth `d ago` branch and tails to `toLocaleDateString()`; `PointInTimeRestore` stops at hours and tails to `toLocaleString()`. The card *body* said this ("the same, minus the days branch") — the title and both PM comments generalised it.

This is what **decides ruling #3 by measurement**: sharing is declined on two independent grounds — the tails are genuinely different, so unifying them would silently restyle one surface, *and* a shared helper is a new export, i.e. Clause ② with the quota exhausted. Reported, not routed around.

### Assumptions confirmed

- **A3.1 — confirmed, sha named.** Head is `d8ec8d6d4`, PR #7162's landing sha; `check:i18n-drift` independently re-derived the same merge-base. Everything was re-derived on it.
- **A3.3 — confirmed, and every mapping is EXACT.** No copy change hid in the swap: `just now`, `{{count}}m ago`, `{{count}}h ago`, `{{count}}d ago` are byte-identical to the literals replaced. (Reported as required rather than quietly adopted: one deliberate copy change does exist, but in the *other* file — `PointInTimeRestore`'s snapshot null placeholder was an EN DASH `–` U+2013 inline and now resolves `detail.emptyValue`, an EM DASH `—` U+2014 in all ten packs, the glyph the rest of the package uses.)
- **A3.5 — confirmed, attributed rather than counted.** Repo-wide hits for `'just now'` / `'m ago'` span five packages; every test assertion among them belongs to `packages/collaboration` (different package and namespace) or to #7162's `ActivityTimeline.remainingLiterals.i18n.test.tsx`. The two `plugin-detail` hits in `RecordMetaFooter.tsx` are **comments**, not literals. Each `PointInTimeRestore` literal has exactly one hit: the file itself. Nothing pinned either file's English.

### A3.4 — reachability, the finding that could have split this card

**`PointInTimeRestore` has zero in-repo consumers.** Repo-wide (excluding `node_modules`/`dist`) it appears only in its own file and twice in the package barrel — `index.tsx:126` export, `:154` type export. Nothing renders it: not `DetailView`, not `apps/console`. `RecordComments` by contrast is rendered by `DetailView` at `:1479` and `:1705`.

So the user-visible defect today is `RecordComments` alone. I still swept `PointInTimeRestore` whole rather than deferring it: it is exported public API a downstream consumer can mount, and finishing it now is what prevents a third #7142-shaped half-done component. Flagging the measurement because it is the kind of thing that legitimately re-splits a card — if you would rather that file had been left alone, the split is clean and the revert is one file plus its keys.

### Pack verification method

Read out of the **pack objects** by walking the nested path (`locales/index.ts` then `builtInLocales`), never a dotted-key grep — the `detail` namespace is one of five in these packs carrying a `justNow` row, so a line grep cannot tell them apart. Loader liveness printed every run: `locales loaded: en,zh,ja,ko,de,fr,es,pt,ru,ar (count=10)`. Positive controls `detail.back` and `detail.noActivity` = 10/10; negative control `detail.zzzAbsentControl7163` = **0/10**. Four existing keys 10/10; ten new keys 10/10 after the change, with both controls re-run in the same invocation and unchanged.

### Carried-forward traps, each honoured

Static `t()` call sites only — the field-count plural is a **static ternary over two literal keys**, never `t(KEYS[n])`. `{{count}}` and `{{when}}` spelled with no inner spaces, and the **provider-less leg is asserted** in both suites (that is where a wrong spelling renders raw and silently). No inline `defaultValue` anywhere. The restore confirmation became **one key with a `{{when}}` hole** rather than a sentence assembled around a JSX expression.

## ✅ LANDED — PR #7172 squash-merged to `main` (`899730e0a`)

Verified **by content with live controls**:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| SUBJECT — `t('detail.justNow')` call site in `RecordComments.tsx` | **1** (and in `PointInTimeRestore.tsx`: 1) |
| SUBJECT — old literal `return 'just now';` in `plugin-detail/src/` | **0** |
| SUBJECT — `Revision History` literal in `PointInTimeRestore.tsx` | **0** |
| PACK — `justNow` / `minutesAgo` | **10 / 10** pack files each |
| PACK CONTROL — `back`, `noActivity` | **10 / 10** each |
| PACK NEG CONTROL — `zzzAbsentControl7163` | **0 / 10** |

### ⚠️ One of my probes was broken, and the discipline this card's own PR taught is what caught it

My first pack control grepped `packages/i18n/src/locales/index.ts` — the **barrel** — and returned **empty**. Read as a zero, that says "the packs do not carry these keys," which would have contradicted a landing that is in fact clean. The packs are ten sibling files in that directory (`ar` `de` `en` `es` `fr` `ja` `ko` `pt` `ru` `zh`); the barrel is not one of them.

⇒ **An empty output is not a `0`** — it is "this probe returned nothing", which includes "this probe was pointed at the wrong thing." The two *legitimate* zeros above are readable only because `t('detail.justNow')` returned counts in the **same command, same path scope**; the pack zeros are readable only after the re-probe produced a positive control and a negative control in one invocation. That is exactly the method this PR used on the packs, and it is why the PR's own reading was trustworthy where my first one was not.

## What landed

**`RecordComments`** — a pure lookup swap onto `detail.justNow` / `minutesAgo` / `hoursAgo` / `daysAgo`, all four already 10/10, every `en` value byte-exact to the literal it replaced. No new key, no copy change.

**`PointInTimeRestore`** — swept **whole**, 17 static `t()` sites, zero English literals left; ten new `detail.*` keys in all ten packs and in `DETAIL_DEFAULT_TRANSLATIONS`; `detail.cancel`, `detail.activityEmptyValue` and `detail.emptyValue` **reused rather than forked**.

## ⭐ The ablation is the best-formed one this seat reviewed this week

Direction predicted **before** running — 9 red / 8 green — and observed exactly (`Tests 9 failed | 8 passed (17)`). What makes it more than a lucky match is *why* it was predictable: every `en` pack value is byte-identical to the literal it replaced, so `en` and provider-less assertions stay green **by construction** while `zh`/`ar` go red. That turns the 8 passes into the instrument proving this was a **lookup swap and not a copy change** — the claim an i18n PR most needs to establish and most easily fakes.

Two traps it navigated that this seat has fallen into:
- **`git checkout -- <path>` restores from the INDEX**, which the mutation had already written. Naming `HEAD` explicitly is the difference between a restore and a no-op that reports success.
- Restore proven **by state** (`git diff HEAD` 0 lines, `git status --porcelain` 0 lines, on-disk hashes equal to HEAD blobs); mutation proven by blob hash **and** marker count on both files.

`--listFiles` also confirmed both new suites are **in** the type-check program (1 hit each, control `zzzNoSuchFile.tsx` = 0), so the green covers them rather than silently excluding them.

## Three judgement calls, all ruled at review and all upheld

1. **`premise_still_valid: false` for A3.2 only.** The "byte-identical copies" claim was false — `RecordComments` has a fourth `d ago` branch and falls through to `toLocaleDateString()`; `PointInTimeRestore` stops at hours and uses `toLocaleString()`. A revision list wants the time of day; a comment list does not. That **decided the sharing question by measurement**: unifying them would silently restyle one surface.
2. **The EN DASH → EM DASH copy change** (U+2013 → `detail.emptyValue`, U+2014). A user-visible copy change riding an i18n card — accepted because the alternative was forking a second `emptyValue` key into ten packs, the multi-spelling class #7021 is paying down. ⭐ Reporting it rather than quietly adopting it is what made it acceptable; an unreported glyph swap inside a 15-file diff is invisible to review.
3. **`PointInTimeRestore` has ZERO in-repo consumers** and was swept whole anyway. Upheld — it is exported public API and a third #7142-shaped half-done component is the worse outcome. But the measurement is more consequential than a scope note, so it is filed as **#7175**: this PR executed ADR-0049's *enforce* half without anyone asking whether *remove* was right. ⛔ #7175 carries a hard limit — "zero in-repo consumers" is **not** "zero consumers", and this seat cannot read `hotcrm` or `cloud`.

## Out-of-scope handling, correct on both

- **#7173** — a fifth copy of the helper in `plugin-chatbot` with genuinely different behaviour (`Math.round` not `Math.floor`, 45s/30d thresholds). Filed with the note that this is *not drift to normalise away*, which is what stops someone "fixing" it into a bug later.
- **#7174** — five near-copies now span two packages. ⭐ Sharing one **is Clause ② by construction** (a helper importable across packages is a new export) and the fable quota is exhausted, so it was **recorded, not acted on**. The observation that `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` may beat sharing the hand-rolled version at all is worth more than the dedup itself.

Clearing `pm:dispatched`.
